- Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter (relation_statistics_helper.cpp).

issues.title: Large perfect hash aggregate (up to 22 bits) with parallel combine and source
issues.hypothesis: In q13 (644ms, 16% of total) the inner HASH_GROUP_BY on c_custkey (1.5M dense groups, stats range 1..1.5M which is about 21 bits) takes 2.13s CPU, the largest operator in the plan. CanUsePerfectHashAggregate (plan_aggregate.cpp:127) rejects it because the total bits exceed perfect_ht_threshold, so it falls back to the radix HT with hashing, probing and partitioned finalize. A previous run on this codebase measured q13 -18.6% (706->576ms) and, re-implemented on top of the RIGHT perfect-HJ base, q13 -24.5% (646->488ms). In that run the larger threshold alone gave only -3.6%, because PerfectAggregateHashTable Combine and the PhysicalPerfectHashAggregate source were serial over 2M slots, which also made the downstream pipeline single-threaded. Both had to be parallelised.
issues.plan: 1) plan_aggregate.cpp CanUsePerfectHashAggregate: allow total bits up to 22 when (a) the estimated input cardinality >= slots/2 (dense enough), and (b) slots * tuple_size * (threads+1) <= max_memory/8. Otherwise keep the existing perfect_ht_threshold rule. 2) perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp Combine: let several threads combine their local tables into the global one at the same time, using striped locks over slot ranges (for example 64 stripes) instead of one global lock. Combine aggregate states using the source (local) arena allocator, then move it into the global table (TakeAllocator) under the global lock. 3) physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp source: make GetData parallel. Global source state hands out blocks of slots through an atomic cursor, each thread scans its block, and MaxThreads returns slots/block_size. Check that ScanAll can start at a given offset (or add a range scan). Keep the result order unspecified, as with hash agg.
issues.expected_gain: q13 -18..-25% (about -1.5% geomean). Possibly other group-bys on dense integer keys with 2^16..2^22 range (custkey/partkey/suppkey-style keys).
issues.generality: Any GROUP BY on one or more integer columns whose combined stats range is up to 4M slots and dense relative to the input, such as FK-keyed aggregates after joins. Risk of slowdown: a sparse range with a small input, which the density guard prevents. Also many threads each allocating a 4M-slot local table, which the memory guard limits.
issues.risk: Medium. The parallel combine must be race-free (stripes must be disjoint slot ranges, and the allocator move must happen under the lock). The source change must cover every slot exactly once. Test against SET perfect_ht_threshold=0 / disabled perfect agg, and compare count/sum/min/max/string aggregates and NULL groups on TEMP tables with 1-4M dense keys.
